findings.title: `upsampled_count` is only registered for the discover dataset but is applied to the errors dataset
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is added only to `DiscoverDatasetConfig.function_converter` in `discover.py`. However `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` returns `True` unconditionally when `dataset is errors`, so for `?dataset=errors` requests the endpoint will send `upsampled_count() as count` to a builder backed by `ErrorsDatasetConfig`, which maintains its own independent `function_converter`. If that config does not also register `upsampled_count`, every errors-dataset timeseries request from an allowlisted project will fail with `InvalidSearchQuery: upsampled_count() is not a valid function` (HTTP 400) instead of returning data. Either register the function for the errors dataset config too, or restrict the transform to datasets that actually expose it. Note that the added tests only exercise the default (discover) dataset, so this path is completely uncovered.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is computed from the outer `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` actually queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as its first parameter and executes the query against it, but the eligibility check passes the enclosing `dataset` variable: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (`discover` for the errors-only probe, `scoped_dataset` for the original), so the transform decision can be made for the wrong dataset: e.g. the errors-only probe against `discover` is evaluated with `dataset == metrics_enhanced_performance` (never upsampled), and conversely a query executed against a non-error dataset can be evaluated as `discover`. The result is counts that are inconsistently upsampled (or a transform sent to a dataset lacking `upsampled_count`). Pass `scoped_dataset` instead.

findings.title: Error-focus detection reads the raw request query instead of the query actually executed
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query()` inspects `request.GET["query"]`, but the query string that is actually executed is passed into `_get_event_stats` as the `query` argument and can differ from the request parameter. In the dashboard split path the endpoint builds `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` (error-only) and `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"` (transaction-only); both are evaluated using the same unmodified `request.GET["query"]`. So an error-only split query will not be upsampled unless the user happened to type `event.type:error`, and a transaction-only split query *will* be upsampled if the user's original query contained `event.type:error`, summing `sample_weight` over transactions where the column does not exist. The detection should operate on the query string handed to the dataset, not on the request parameter.

findings.title: Cross-request cache of allowlist eligibility is stale, never invalidated, and keyed by `hash()`
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist decision in the shared cache for 60s under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org_id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`. Three problems: (1) the option value `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is not part of the key and `invalidate_upsampling_cache()` is dead code (no caller anywhere in this PR), so after an operator changes the allowlist—including turning it off because counts are wrong—requests keep returning 10x-inflated or non-upsampled counts for up to 60s with no way to flush; (2) `options.get` is already backed by an option cache, so this adds a correctness window for no measurable gain; (3) using `hash()` of the project-id tuple makes different project sets collide into the same key, which silently applies the wrong upsampling decision (use a deterministic, collision-free key such as the sorted ids joined by commas).

findings.title: `sum(sample_weight)` silently returns 0 for events without a sample weight
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count()`, which is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. The docstring asserts "we rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists", but a project only gets a `sample_rate`/`sample_weight` once the SDK sends `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`; events ingested before upsampling was enabled, events from SDKs that do not send it, and events from other event sources in the same (allowlisted) project will have a NULL/0 weight. For those rows `sum(sample_weight)` contributes 0 instead of 1, so adding a project to the allowlist silently zeroes or undercounts historical and non-instrumented error counts in charts and alerts. The aggregate should fall back to 1 per row when `sample_weight` is absent (e.g. `sum(if(sample_weight > 0, sample_weight, 1))` or an equivalent coalesce).

findings.title: `upsampled_count` is exposed as a public discover function
findings.body: Unlike the neighbouring internal helper functions, the new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is not marked `private=True`, so any API consumer can request `field=upsampled_count()`/`yAxis=upsampled_count()` on discover/transaction queries. Since it compiles to `sum(sample_weight)` and `sample_weight` does not exist for transaction rows, this is a user-reachable path to a raw Snuba/ClickHouse "unknown column" error (500/snuba error surfaced to the client), and it becomes an unintentionally supported public API surface. Also, the aggregate returns `toInt64(...)` but declares `default_result_type="number"`; `"integer"` matches the actual value type and the result type reported for `count()`.

findings.title: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` swallows all exceptions, hiding mis-set sample rates
findings.body: Both the context lookup and the `float()` conversion are wrapped in bare `except Exception: pass`, and invalid/zero values are dropped by the `if client_sample_rate:` guard. If a test supplies a malformed `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`, `sample_rate` is silently not set and the stored event gets `sample_weight = 1`; the upsampling assertions (e.g. `count == 10`) then fail with no indication of why. Let the conversion raise (or assert) so test authors get an actionable error instead of a mysterious count mismatch.

findings.title: No test covers the public entry point or its caching behaviour
findings.body: The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and the column transform. `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — the only function the endpoint actually calls, and the one containing the new 60s shared-cache logic — is never tested, nor is `invalidate_upsampling_cache`. As a result, the cache-hit path (including the `cached_result is not None` handling of a cached `False`, and the key-building logic duplicated between the two functions) is unverified, and regressions in the caching layer would silently change query results in production.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR's own base commit) with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly a local workspace artifact: it makes `git submodule update`/`git clone --recurse-submodules` fail or warn about an uninitialized submodule with no URL, and pollutes the repo tree. It must be removed before merging.

findings.title: New file violates the repo's formatting rules (will fail lint/CI)
findings.body: `pyproject.toml` configures black/flake8 with `line-length = 100`, but the `cache_key` assignment on this line is ~110 characters, and the new file plus the edits in `organization_events_stats.py` contain trailing whitespace on several blank/comment lines (e.g. after `should_upsample = ...` and inside the docstrings). Pre-commit/black and flake8 will reject the diff as-is; run the formatter before merging.
